message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

permissions: read-all

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup PNPM
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Run tests
        run: pnpm test",
  "rationale": "The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by measured CI workflow experiments showing elapsed savings when jobs are given an explicit timeout budget (timeout-minutes: 5), with measured elapsed reductions of 26.8% and 9.8% and no loss of required checks. The repository satisfies the precondition: CI history shows representative successful runs of roughly 27-39 seconds. The current job already bounds execution but at 10 minutes, about 17x the observed median; lowering it to 5 minutes still provides roughly 8x headroom over observed runs while halving the maximum runaway consumption. All build and test steps are preserved unchanged, so intended coverage is retained. Dependency caching is already present via setup-node cache: pnpm, so P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is contraindicated (equivalent cache exists), and no matrix exists for fail-fast/cancel-stale patterns.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8"]
}
